builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
summary: DFly2 replaces a speculative drafter's independent KV cache and context-selection logic with direct reuse of the target model's cached KV pairs and the target's own per-layer sparse index selections, eliminating the drafter's cache, its prefill cost, and any scoring pass. The cost is tight coupling to a natively sparse target architecture with a paired indexer, plus drafter retraining per target model, and it adds no benefit on dense-attention models. It can fail when deployed targets lack native sparse attention, when the one-step-stale index selection degrades on shifting workloads, or when the reader's serving stack cannot expose the target's internal index selections to the drafter.
rationale: The method requires a natively sparse target model with an index-based selection mechanism and a block-parallel drafter trained against that specific architecture, which is not a component the reader can adopt or fine-tune on a single 24 GB GPU.
technique: Speculative drafting sharing target's sparse attention indices

claims.statement: DFly2 replaces a speculative drafter's independent KV cache and context-selection logic with direct reuse of the target model's cached KV pairs and the target's own per-layer sparse index selections, eliminating the drafter's cache, its prefill cost, and any scoring pass. The cost is tight coupling to a natively sparse target architecture with a paired indexer, plus drafter retraining per target model, and it adds no benefit on dense-attention models. It can fail when deployed targets lack native sparse attention, when the one-step-stale index selection degrades on shifting workloads, or when the reader's serving stack cannot expose the target's internal index selections to the drafter.

At high concurrency on DS-V4.1-Flash, at matched per-user decode speed, throughput is 62% and 81% higher on two 64K sets; acceptance rates exceed the stronger baseline by 3.9%-10.5% on general workloads and 10.0%-31.5% on long-context and agentic workloads.
